Title: Atelier — Model Pragmatics: Adaptive Quant & Prompt Pipeline (Annotated notes)
Summary:
- Field-lab notes from a week-long POC with a telecom customer exploring a hybrid ensemble approach: lightweight 7B quant model + heavy 70B float variant, with per-request precision scoring and adaptive routing.
- Goal: keep 95p latency < 500ms for interactive chat while holding quality degradation under an agreed threshold (per-turn semantic-similarity >= 0.88 against reference set) and minimizing cost (target: < 0.18 USD per 1k tokens net).
- This doc captures rationale, experimental matrix, prompt/pipeline heuristics, and an initial canary rollout playbook.
- Status: experiments done in lab; still need infra config validation for Private customer VPC and SLO guardrails.
Context / customer constraints:
- Telecom partner needs on-device-style responsiveness for CX agents; PII considered sensitive; they prefer Private deployment into their VPC but requested an expedited Hosted proof for time-to-value.
- Throughput: expected bursty traffic (peak concurrency ~180 sessions) with average session length 40 turns.
- Acceptable failure modes: degraded quality (fallback to human) preferred over exposing hallucinated statements.
High-level approach (why different):
- Ensemble on inference path: run a small quantized model (Q) as primary for every request; compute a lightweight quality estimator; escalate to large model (F) only when estimator predicts below threshold OR request tagged as high-risk (billing, legal, escalation).
- Estimator must be cheap and robust: small model scoring + lexical/semantic heuristics, not an expensive reranker.
- Leverage KV-prefix caching for sessions (chat history) and prefix-similarity caching to avoid repeated full-decodes on repetitive prompts.
- Route-by-policy in Redwood: latency-first for consumer queries, precision-first for escalations. Use automatic fallback to F when Q returns low-confidence or safety flags.
Experiment matrix done (summary):
- Models tested: q7b-4bit (static 4-bit quant, GPT-style), q7b-int8 (dynamic 8-bit), f70b-fp16 (high-quality float), f13b-pt (13B float tuned via instruction tuning baseline).
- Prompt families: terse prompts (<=120 tokens), context-rich (full 6-turn history), doc-grounded (includes customer KB chunk). Also tried structured prompt with explicit answer schema.
- Metrics collected: response-latency P50/P95/P99, token-cost estimates, top-1 semantic sim (SBERT) against small reference set (150 labeled examples), and safety flag rate.
- Key result: q7b-4bit + estimator routing hit median latency 230ms, P95 ~ 480ms; overall quality delta vs f70b ~ -0.07 (semantic sim). Routing saved ~62% cost vs always-F.
- Failure cases: knowledge-intensive doc-grounded answers often dropped below similarity threshold; hallucination rate non-negligible for long-context retrieval if KB chunking not aligned with model tokenization.
Quality estimator design (lightweight):
- Components:
  1) Quick-forward: run q7b to get early logits + reply candidate. Compute token-level logprob average as confidence baseline.
  2) Semantic-sim proxy: embed input+candidate via small embed model (c2-small) and compute cosine with cached reference embeddings for that bucket.
  3) Heuristic checks: token-length delta vs prompt length, presence of OOV tokens, deterministic dates/numeric checks for consistency.
- Scoring: weighted sum (logprob * 0.6 + embed-sim * 0.3 + heuristic_score * 0.1). Thresholds tuned on labeled dev set (precision-oriented; false-negatives cost more than false-positives for escalations).
- Implementation note: estimator must run within 15–25ms on the same GPU to avoid adding >10% latency. We evaluated moving estimator to CPU but GPU co-location reduced context transfer overhead.
Prompt and pipeline heuristics (practica:
- Shorten system prompt tokens for Q; keep critical instructions only. Use full system instructions for F to maximize quality.
- Canonicalize user timestamps/dates before feed to models to reduce hallucination anchors.
- Chunk KB by semantic passages aligned to 250–300 token blocks (post-tokenizer) rather than raw paragraph splits.
- Use structured output for action items (JSON schema) for both Q and F; compare parse success as additional confidence signal.
- Prefix caching: store last-turn KV per session; if next request shares >70% n-gram overlap with recent prefix, attempt prefix-rewrite to reuse KV rather than re-encoding.
Quantization observations and tradeoffs:
- q7b-4bit (static) gave best cost profile but increased rare-token hallucinations on doc-grounded prompts.
- q7b-int8 (dynamic) reduced hallucination at modest cost increase and was often a sweet spot for latency-sensitive-but-knowledge tasks.
- f13b-pt served as midline: reduced escalation rate but at ~2.5x token cost vs q7b-int8.
- Recommendation: default primary = q7b-int8 with fallback to f13b-pt for mid-tier and f70b-fp16 for critical escalation. Offer q7b-4bit as experimental low-cost variant for very latency-sensitive paths.
Decisions and rationale (short list):
- Default routing policy: q7b-int8 primary, estimator threshold tuned for 92% precision on dev set. Escalation => f13b-pt, then f70b-fp16 if f13b flagged low-confidence.
- Safety policy: any safety flag from Q triggers immediate escalation to F (do not attempt auto-edit).
- Cost SLO: cap average token spend per session and emit alerts when 3-day rolling average exceeds budget.
Canary rollout plan (Redwood routes + co:
1) Create two routes in Redwood Console: "telecom-poc-primary" (q7b-int8) and "telecom-poc-escalation" (f13b-pt/f70b-fp16 fallback). Configure prefix caching TTL 30m per session.
2) Start with 5% traffic (internal canary) for 48 hours; monitor P95 latency and escalation rate. Stop if P95 > 600ms or escalation > 25%.
3) Gradually increase to 25% over 3 days if KPIs stable. Maintain daily manual review of 50 sampled escalations.
4) Add A/B variant with q7b-4bit for 10% of traffic to collect low-cost telemetry.
Infra and deployment notes (Private comp:
- VPC: ensure private control plane has access only to telemetry sink; inference instances must remain in customer VPC and connect to control via mutual TLS.
- KMS: store model keys and encryption with HSM option; confirm export restrictions for any third-party models.
- Autoscaling: configure min 20 pods for q7b-int8 pool and burst node pool for f13b/f70b. Pre-warm f13b pool during business hours to reduce cold-start penalties.
- Observability: capture per-request route, estimator_score, model_variant, KV-cache-hit boolean, and safety_flags. Retain traces for 30 days for initial analysis.
Open questions / unknowns:
- How to calibrate estimator across languages (customer uses EN and FR). Embedding sim thresholds likely language-dependent — need per-lang dev sets.
- Edge-case: multi-document syntheses where required context > 4k tokens — policy: do retrieval-summary chunking, but we need to measure summary drift.
- Pricing sensitivity: customer has internal threshold for monthly inference spend — need to model cost under realistic traffic traces (ask finance to run 90th percentile billing projection).
Next steps (action items):

- R2 (Mateo): implement Redwood route configs and deploy q7b-int8 pool in hosted test environment. ETA 2025-12-05.
- R3 (Rina): prepare sampling dashboard (50 escalations/day) and label interface for SME review. ETA 2025-12-08.

Appendix \u2014 sample prompt snippets /:
- Primary prompt (Q):
  "system: You are an assistant that returns short, factual answers. If unsure, respond \"I don't know — escalate\". user: {user_text}\ncontext: {kb_chunk}\n" 
- Fallback prompt (F): full-instruction long-form with cite-anchors + answer schema (JSON: {"answer","sources"]).
- Estimator thresholds (dev-tuned):
  - logprob_avg > -1.8
  - embed_sim > 0.875
  - combined_score > 0.89 => accept
Notes to self:
- Watch out for KB chunk tokenizer misalignment; run tokenizer-based chunker in the preprocessor (not naive char-split).
- Try combining estimator with cheap lexical reranker (n-gram overlap) to catch retrieval misses quickly.

End of notes.
